issues.description: Constructor signature for class SealSaloon is inconsistent between the problem statement and the provided code. The UML and the textual description in the problem statement require a constructor SealSaloon(String) that accepts a saloon name (problem_statement.md: UML line declaring +SealSaloon(String) and text saying "The constructor takes the saloon name as a String parameter"). However, both the template Main (template repository) and the reference solution implement and use a no-argument constructor SealSaloon() (Template Main usage: 'new SealSaloon()'; Solution SealSaloon: 'public SealSaloon()'). This mismatch will confuse students about which constructor to implement and may result in submission or testing failures if tests expect the alternate signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across all artifacts. Option A (preferred if name is not needed): update the problem statement and UML to specify a no-argument constructor SealSaloon(), removing the requirement to pass/store a saloon name. Option B (if name is intended): change the template Main and the solution to instantiate and implement SealSaloon(String name) (add a private final String name field, set it in the constructor, and add a getter). Update the UML, textual description, example Main, and the reference solution so all four artifacts use the same constructor signature.

issues.description: The declaration and intended semantics of the stock attribute for SealSaloon are inconsistent in the problem statement. Earlier in the problem text it describes a 'final Stock stock' to be initialized in the constructor (implying a per-instance final field). Later the spec explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across all instances): "Note that the following methods and attributes must be static: - stock attribute" (problem_statement.md). The reference solution implements the field as a static class-level field 'private static final Stock stock = new Stock();' (solution SealSaloon). This contradiction (per-instance final vs. static shared) will confuse students about whether to implement stock as an instance final field or as a static class field.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended design in the problem statement and make code/examples follow it. If stock should be shared across all saloons, explicitly state that and keep the implementation as 'private static final Stock stock = new Stock();' and document that it is shared. If stock should be per-instance and final, remove the 'static' requirement from the problem statement, update the UML/text accordingly, and change the reference solution and any example usage to use a non-static 'private final Stock stock' initialized in the constructor (and adjust acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice to be instance methods or call the instance stock appropriately). Ensure the template Main and tests reflect the chosen design.
